tier_reason: Benchmark code is public (bench/rawdec.c for the raw-decode table, bench/formatdec.c and bench/formats.sh for the charts), CMakeLists.txt sets Release -O3 without -march=native, and docs/BENCHMARKS.md names gcc 16.1.1/16.2.1 and an Intel Pentium B960; rawdec memcmp-checks PXL's output against the source pixels on every repetition and libpng returns the same 8-bit layout. It is a format-versus-format comparison, tiered A like the Zpng entry's qoir comparison.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Raw-pixel decode of the 24 Kodak photographs (bench/rawdec, median of 15 runs per file, summed, single thread): libpng 333.6 ms vs PXL 143.2 ms, about 2.3x (README). PXL files are 85.5% of the PNG bytes. QOI is faster still at 120.7 ms, but its files are 103.5% of the PNG bytes. An earlier logged run measured libpng 347.5 ms vs PXL 163.7 ms (2.1x). In-process decode to RGBA8888 (bench/formatdec.c, BENCHMARKS.md 2026-09-16 correction): on 24 photographs libpng runs at 98.6 MB/s, against PXL level 1 at 275.8 MB/s (87.8% of PNG size), level 12 at 199.6 MB/s (88.6%) and level 19 at 226.7 MB/s (85.6%), i.e. 2.0x to 2.8x (derived from page data). On 30 synthetic stills libpng runs at 308.7 MB/s, against PXL at 449.8 to 536.7 MB/s (1.5x to 1.7x, derived from page data), while WebP is both faster (570.2 MB/s) and smaller (44.6% vs PXL's best 50.3%). On a real PSP-3008: none and delta beat libpng by 2.8x to 3.5x, and BCIF by 2.94x at 480x272. adaptive ties libpng (1.01x to 1.02x). BCIF loses at 512x512 texture size (0.54x).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 16.1.1 (July 2026 log entries) and gcc 16.2.1 (from the 2026-09-15 README regeneration on). CMake Release with CMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELEASE -O3 (CMakeLists.txt; confirmed in flags.make per BENCHMARKS.md), no -march=native, no LTO. libpng 1.6.x is linked from the system by default, with zlib dynamic. VERSIONS.json pins libpng 1.6.59 and zstd 1.5.7 for the vendored CI build. The exact libpng/zlib build behind the README run is not recorded.
corrections.license: libpng-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause (files under ffmpeg/ are FFmpeg patch material under LGPL-2.1-or-later)
corrections.workload: bench/rawdec.c on the 24 Kodak photographs, single thread, median of 15 runs per file, summed over files. PXL decodes an in-memory .pxl encoded at zstd level 12 (the default level is 1). libpng decodes a PNG that pxl_save_png re-encoded with libpng's default write settings, read back through pxl_load_png. Both produce native 8-bit RGB. bench/formatdec.c decodes in process to RGBA8888 for the size-versus-speed charts (24 Kodak photographs and 30 synthetic stills) against libpng, QOI, WebP, JPEG XL and AVIF, all single-threaded. Separate libpng comparison on a real PSP-3008 with one synthetic pattern at 480x272 and 512x512.
corrections.caveats: A distinct codec, not a fork or port of Zpng as a whole: it has its own PXL1 container, palette and 1- to 16-bit support, adaptive PNG row filters, metadata pass-through, streaming and animation. Only the delta and BCIF colour-plane filters are ported from Zpng (catid/Zpng, already catalogued; its BSD-3 notice is retained). On the Kodak photographs BCIF wins all 24 files (BENCHMARKS.md 2026-07-29), so the headline photo decode path is Zpng's transform plus zstd in C. The comparison is format versus format: libpng decodes a PNG while PXL decodes a .pxl re-encoded from it. PXL is therefore not a faster PNG decoder, and existing PNGs must be converted first. In bench/rawdec.c the libpng side is timed through pxl_load_png. That function reads the file from disk (page cache) and scans its chunks for metadata before decoding, while PXL decodes from a memory buffer: a small bias against libpng. The README's raw-decode timings are not logged in BENCHMARKS.md, and the author says timing columns are not comparable across runs. The benchmark machine is a 2-core Pentium B960 that the author reports carries about 35% background load even when idle. QOI is about 16% faster than PXL on 24 of 24 files. Every decoder runs single-threaded, and libjxl and libavif get no worker threads. An earlier chart overstated PXL by 4/3 (3-channel output counted as 4) until all decoders were forced to RGBA8 on 2026-09-16. On synthetic stills WebP is smaller and faster. On the PSP the adaptive filter only ties libpng, and BCIF is 0.54x libpng at texture size (one synthetic pattern measured). 7 stars.

notes: Decided not a duplicate of Zpng: it is a new format and library that ports only Zpng's delta and BCIF filters, although on the Kodak photographs the decoded path is Zpng's BCIF in all 24 files. Numbers match the README and BENCHMARKS.md. Two corrections: the record paired the level-19 size (85.6%) with the 200-276 MB/s range across all levels, and its PSP summary left out BCIF's 0.54x loss at texture size.

tier_reason: First-party evidence. bench/bench.mjs is public and the CPU is named (Apple M1 Max, macOS 12.3.1). The addon is a prebuilt binary with no compiler or flags, the Node, sharp and package versions were not recorded, and the README itself calls the table historical rather than a benchmark of 1.15.0.

corrections.workload: bench/bench.mjs: one EXIF JPEG (with-exif.jpg, exif-samples portrait_5.jpg) is rotated by its EXIF orientation, resized to width 225 with the image crate's Lanczos3 resize, and encoded to WebP (quality 75) or AVIF (quality 70, 4:2:0). Up to 10,000 iterations or 20 s are submitted concurrently up to the CPU count, and throughput is iterations over wall time. sharp runs the same chain, ending in .toBuffer().
corrections.caveats: A Node.js binding (napi-rs) over Rust and C codec libraries, not a codec of its own. In the benchmarked pipeline, JPEG decode (zune-jpeg) and the Lanczos3 resize run in the image crate 0.25. The bench calls resize, not the fast_image_resize path. WebP encode is libwebp via libwebp-sys (WebPEncodeRGB/RGBA), and AVIF encode is libavif with libaom (speed 5). sharp uses the same libwebp and libaom through libvips and libheif, so the measured 1.08x to 1.8x reflects decode, resize and scheduling differences, not a faster encoder. fast_image_resize and oxipng (both catalogued) are bound but not exercised by this bench. The table was recorded on macOS 12.3.1 (2022 era). The repo now pins sharp ^0.35.2 as a devDependency, but the sharp, Node and @napi-rs/image versions behind the numbers are unknown. The bench uses a single input image and makes no output-size or quality comparison; the README notes that equal numeric quality does not mean equal visual quality. The 1.8x applies only to WebP with UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=10. The default-pool WebP row is 1.20x and the AVIF rows are 1.08x and 1.13x (derived from page data). The baseline sharp is itself recorded as a duplicate of libvips; libwebp and libavif are not compared directly.

notes: Numbers match the README table exactly. Not folded as a duplicate: the benchmarked work runs in the image crate, libwebp and libaom, none of which is catalogued (only zune-image's workspace is), though the orchestrator may still treat it as a wrapper like @napi-rs/canvas. The encoders are the same C libraries sharp uses, so this is pipeline and concurrency evidence, not a faster codec. Metadata checked: MIT, 417 stars, last commit 2026-09-30, not a fork.

tier_reason: First-party harness: benches/vs_image.rs and BENCH.md, with release profile lto=fat, codegen-units=1 and a named Xeon Platinum 8272CL. The rustc version is not stated (only MSRV 1.85), the Apple M-series model is not named, and timing is one batch of 50 iterations (mean) with no statistics.

corrections.baseline: Rust image crate 0.25: its own built-in scalar JPEG encoder (4:2:0 only) and its zune-jpeg-backed decoder. libjpeg-turbo is never measured.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: cargo bench --bench vs_image with release profile lto = "fat", codegen-units = 1; SIMD build with runtime-dispatched AVX2 / NEON kernels. rustc version not stated (crate MSRV 1.85, edition 2024, no pinned toolchain file).
corrections.workload: benches/vs_image.rs. Encode: 3-byte RGB of the synthetic XOR full-AC pattern only, q=80, at 1592x1124, 1080p and 4K, with threads=1 and threads=auto on jpeg-rusturbo's side; image is single-threaded and 4:2:0-only, so only the 4:2:0 rows compare like with like. Decode: jpeg-rusturbo's own q=80 4:2:0 output, decoded to RGB, on the synthetic and natural-like generated images. Each figure is the mean of one batch of 50 iterations after 3 warm-ups.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 0 stars; crates.io jpeg-rusturbo 0.9.2, 7,763 downloads in total (7,617 of them on 0.9.2)
corrections.caveats: There is no comparison with libjpeg-turbo or mozjpeg anywhere. The baseline is the image crate, whose built-in encoder is scalar and 4:2:0-only; the vs_image.rs header names image's own encoder, not the jpeg-encoder crate. The 5x single-thread and 6.9x to 10x threads=auto encode wins therefore say nothing about libjpeg-turbo. The threads=auto rows also set a rayon-parallel encoder against a single-threaded one. Per NOTICE.md, the encoder's four hot kernels (colour conversion, 4:2:0 downsample, integer forward DCT, quantize) are translated from libjpeg-turbo's NEON/AVX2 SIMD code, and so are the decoder's IDCT, fancy upsample and YCC-to-RGB kernels. In part, then, this is a Rust port of libjpeg-turbo (catalogued). The encode comparison uses only the synthetic XOR full-AC pattern, both sides at q=80, with no output size or quality comparison between the two encoders. In the decode comparison the image side calls ImageReader::decode().to_rgb8(). That adds a full-frame conversion copy (about 24.9 MB at 4K) that jpeg-rusturbo's side does not pay, so part of the 1.18x to 1.22x lead at 4K may be harness overhead. Otherwise decode is at parity with zune-jpeg and slightly slower at 1592x1124 on the Xeon (0.97x to 0.98x); the decode numbers come from an older campaign. Inputs are generated images, not a photo corpus. The Apple host had light background load. Rust (language-filter mismatch).

notes: All claimed numbers match BENCH.md and the README; no libjpeg-turbo number exists. Corrected the baseline label: the encoder is image's own, not jpeg-encoder. The kernels are translated from libjpeg-turbo, so the orchestrator may treat this as a partial port of the listed libjpeg-turbo; the precedent libjpeg-turbo-rs was kept. Metadata checked: MIT OR Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-06-08, 0 stars, not a fork.
